key_insight: BAP1, with ASXL3, acts as a transcriptional regulator that remodels the cell surface glycoproteome to reduce alpha-synuclein fibril internalization.
clinical_relevance: This identifies a Parkinson’s disease risk-gene pathway that may help explain and potentially modulate early cellular uptake of pathogenic alpha-synuclein, especially in dopaminergic neurons.
method: Genome-wide CRISPR activation screen to find modifiers of alpha-synuclein fibril uptake
Validation in human cell models, including iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons and microglia
Human midbrain organoids with integrated microglia to test ASXL3-dependent effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports screening plus validation across multiple human model systems, with cell-type-specific reduction of fibril uptake after BAP1 enhancement.
watch_item: The effect appears cell-type specific and was shown in model systems, so translational relevance and therapeutic feasibility need further in vivo validation.
paper_title: The Parkinson 's Disease Associated BAP1/ASXL3 Complex Regulates the Internalization of α-Synuclein Fibrils by Reprogramming the Cell Surface Glycoproteome
